name: Central Park
title: Ancient Trees in Central Park, New York: 7 to Find
meta_description: Central Park's oldest trees: a Mall elm allee that outlived Dutch elm disease, a multi-trunked Reservoir plane, and a 1912 cherry gift from Japan.
intro: Central Park opened in 1858 on land that had no old trees at all: the ground was swamp, rock and scattered farms before Frederick Law Olmsted and Calvert Vaux's Greensward Plan turned 843 acres of Manhattan into the park now walked by tens of millions of people a year. Everything standing today was planted, which makes its oldest survivors a record of what the park's own gardeners chose a century and a half ago, not what nature left behind. Two of these seven trees are American elms from the Mall's Literary Walk, one of the last major stands of the species anywhere after Dutch elm disease wiped out most of the country's street elms starting in the 1930s. A third elm, gnarled and wide canopied at the park's East 97th Street entrance, is old enough that nobody recorded its planting year. Two rival candidates for the park's single oldest tree, a multi-trunked London plane by the Reservoir and a black tupelo in the Ramble, disagree by only four years and neither comes with proof. Between them stands a small grove of Lebanon cedars planted for a family's grandchildren, and 35 Yoshino cherry trees whose planting predates the more famous gift Washington DC received the same year, 1912. All are free to see, every day, dawn to dusk.
